newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends higher, but upside seen limited.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends higher, but upside seen limited.

text.p: CSCE coffee advanced Tuesday on the heels of stock data showing certified coffee inventories at their lowest level in more than a decade, dealers said, but the rally fell short of key resistance targets.

Prices rose from the outset, fueled by a steep, 10,000-bag drop in exchange-deliverable coffee. The drawdown, which caught many traders by surprise, reduced CSCE certified stocks to a 12-year low of 31,669 bags as of September 27.
But the early rally failed to catch fire, and selling by producer countries reappeared toward the highs, dealers said.
Benchmarket December futures rose 1.80 cent per lb, to 104.75, after trading from 103.50 to 105.60.
Today's decidedly measured run-up points to what analysts said is coffee's limited upside potential over the long-term.

With stocks in consumer countries expected to build steadily in the coming months as Latin American producers harvest their 1996/97 crop, buyers will likely become increasingly cautious, said Smith Barney analyst Walter Spilka.
"Coffee prices are not going to go up much more because the coffee harvest is coming," said Smith Barney analyst Walter Spilka. "Pretty soon, we will be knee-deep in coffee."

The nearby December contract benefitted most from the stock draw, padding its premium to second-position March by 0.70 cent. Traders said the switch could widen out to as much as 6.00 cents as coffee roasters seek to secure near-term supplies.
Technically, 107.25 remained a key resistance objective, with downside targets noted at yesterday's low of 102.25 and then at 100.00 cents.
Turnover on the exchange was estimated at 7,906 lots.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
